events.title: Proposed ruling: escalate (model confidence 0.90)
events.body:
This is a rider-filed safety incident: the complaint alleges the driver "kept making comments about my body and asked for my number" and that she "felt harassed and unsafe" [F3][SAFE-1]. That is an allegation of harassment and unwanted sexual advances, which SAFE-1 says must not be auto-decided; the case goes to a human with a factual summary [F3][F4][SAFE-1]. The policy execution trace confirms the SAFE-1 screen is met and the only permitted outcome is escalate.

What happened, when: trip RydeX Woodlands Civic Centre → Punggol Waterway Point, pickup 22:29, drop-off 22:54 [F1][F2]. The in-app chat record is empty: "No in-app chat messages between rider and driver" [F3], so the words the rider attributes to the driver exist nowhere in the record; the driver's written statement says only "I made small talk. Nothing inappropriate happened." [F4]. Both sides agree a conversation took place in the vehicle; its content is unrecorded, which is precisely what SAFE-1 sends to a person to read [F3][F4][SAFE-1].

What is disputed: whether the driver made comments about the rider's body and asked for her number. The record cannot settle it — F3 supplies no contemporaneous message and F4 is the driver's own post-trip statement, not a system record [F3][F4][SAFE-1]. Per the evidence rule, a record gap is not treated as favouring either side, so no automated finding can be made either way [F3][F4][SAFE-1].

Not in dispute and not a basis for any money movement: the trip data show no route deviation — actual 17.2 km against an optimal 17.3 km (-0.1 km) [F1] — and a 2.3-minute duration overrun (25.9 vs 24 min) [F2], ordinary traffic variation, not a dangerous-driving allegation on this record [F1][F2][SAFE-2]. The fare is a fixed quote and no fare fact is in dispute, so no refund is available on any route or fare clause [F1][F2][FARE-1].

Profile facts are attached for the reviewer but decide nothing alone: rider, 3.8 years, 4.8 rating, 0 disputes in 90 d [F5]; driver, 4.5 years, 4.86 rating, 659 trips in 90 d, 0 disputes, 0 upheld [F6]. A clean record does not resolve a word-against-word allegation and is not a basis for automated dismissal, and likewise an unblemished rider profile is not a basis for an automated finding against the driver [F5][F6][SAFE-1]. No account action is ordered here: the account-flag clauses (RD-6, NS-2) are not engaged, since no route refund is due and no 'I'm Here'/no-show issue is in this case [F1][F6][RD-6][NS-2].

actions.detail: Rider-filed harassment/safety complaint (body comments, request for her number, stated feeling of harassment and unsafety) — SAFE-1 requires human review and no automatic ruling; the record is a word-against-word dispute with no in-app chat (F3) and only the driver's post-trip denial (F4), so the content of the spoken exchange cannot be settled from the file.

claims.assertion: The rider's complaint states that the driver 'kept making comments about my body and asked for my number' and that she 'felt harassed and unsafe' — an allegation of harassment and unwanted sexual advances made during the trip, which the driver does not deny in substance, saying only 'I made small talk. Nothing inappropriate happened.'

Because this is a harassment / unwanted-advances allegation, the case must be screened under SAFE-1 and sent to a human: no automated ruling is to be issued, and a fact summary should accompany the escalation. This holds regardless of the outcome of any route or fare analysis.

The chat record contains no in-app messages between rider and driver, so there is no contemporaneous chat evidence either confirming or rebutting the driver's account; when the record cannot determine consent/conduct, that gap supports human review rather than an automated dismissal.

On the objective trip records the ride itself shows no exploitation of the rider while she felt unsafe: actual distance 17.2 km vs optimal 17.3 km (-0.1 km, -0%) with duration 25.9 min vs 24 min estimated (+2.3 min) — so the escalation rests on the safety allegation, not on any proven overcharge or detour.

The rider is a 3.8-year account holder, rating 4.8, with 0 disputes filed in the last 90 days — a history that gives no indication of vexatious or repeat complaining, which supports taking her safety report seriously at human review.

The driver holds a 4.5-year account with 659 trips in 90 days and 0 upheld disputes; this clean history is a point in his favour and must be weighed by the human reviewer, but it cannot resolve a word-on-word harassment allegation and is not a basis for automated dismissal.

weaknesses: The only account of the alleged comments is the rider's complaint; the chat record shows no in-app messages (F3) and the driver's statement (F4) denies anything inappropriate, so there is no corroborating objective record of what was said — the reviewer may find the allegation unproven.

The driver's profile (F6) shows a long-standing account (4.5 years), 4.86 rating and 0 upheld disputes in 90 days, which the other side will use to argue the conduct alleged is out of character and that no account action is warranted.

No fare facts exist for this case and the GPS facts (F1, F2) show the ride was essentially on the optimal route with only a 2.3-minute duration overrun, so the rider cannot support any monetary refund claim — the requested outcome is escalation only, with no amount.

The escalation rests on the rider's own severity description ('felt harassed and unsafe') rather than on admitted words, and a reviewer could treat the rider's framing as subjective while finding the driver's statement credible.

claims.assertion: This is a rider-filed safety complaint alleging body comments and a request for the rider's number (the complaint itself, quoted in the case file), i.e. an allegation of harassment, so on its face the case engages the mandatory human-review screening under SAFE-1 rather than an automated fare ruling.

The only in-app record of what was said between the parties is F3, which states there were no in-app chat messages at all ("No in-app chat messages between rider and driver"), so the chat record contains no threatening, intimidating, harassing or sexually explicit words attributable to my client and supplies no verbal content to support the complaint.

The driver's account that he made only small talk and that nothing inappropriate happened (F4) is unrefuted by any contemporaneous message, since F3 shows the chat record is empty; I ask the judge to weigh that F4 is a written statement given after the trip and, under the system-records-priority rule, no system record corroborates the rider's version either.

The trip itself produced no misconduct evidence of any kind: F1 shows the actual distance was 17.2 km against a 17.3 km optimal route (-0.1 km, -0%), so there is no unexplained route deviation, and F2 shows only a 2.3-minute duration overrun (25.9 vs 24 min), which is ordinary traffic variation, not evidence of dangerous or erratic driving.

My client's record is clean and long-standing: F6 shows a 4.5-year-old account, a 4.86 rating, 659 trips in the last 90 days, and zero disputes and zero upheld complaints of any type in 90 days, so there is no pattern of conduct or prior safety finding that could be used to support an adverse account action against him.

The rider's own profile (F5: 3.8-year account, 4.8 rating, 0 disputes in 90 days) contains no prior complaint history and no corroborating record, which underscores that the sole material in this case is one party's uncorroborated account against the other's denial.

Because the complaint is an harassment allegation and the file contains an empty chat record (F3) that cannot resolve whose account is correct, the appropriate disposition is escalation to a human reviewer with a facts summary, not an automated finding against the driver.

weaknesses: The complaint is itself the primary adverse material: it directly alleges body comments and a request for the rider's number, which is exactly the kind of conduct SAFE-1 covers, and I have no system record that disproves it — F3 is empty only in the sense of containing no in-app messages, not in the sense of proving nothing was said aloud in the vehicle.

My client's denial (F4) is a self-serving statement made after the trip; it is not a system record and the judge may give it little weight against the rider's contemporaneous complaint, and I cannot point to any GPS/chat/timeline fact that contradicts the rider's account (F1, F2 are neutral on conduct, not exculpatory).
The rider's profile is unblemished (F5: 3.8-year account, 4.8 rating, 0 disputes), which undercuts any suggestion that this is a bad-faith or serial complaint.

Nothing in F1-F6 can positively establish that the conversation was appropriate; at best the record is silent, so I cannot ask for a no_action finding on the merits and am limited to seeking escalation rather than dismissal.

points.response: Conceded as far as it goes: I agree the complaint triggers the SAFE-1 human-review screen, which is exactly the escalate outcome I ask for; the only difference is that escalation must carry a facts summary recording the rider's harassment allegation, not just the empty chat record.

The emptiness of the in-app chat (F3) only means the exchange was verbal and therefore unrecorded — it does not mean nothing was said; the driver's own statement (F4) admits he 'made small talk' during the trip, so both sides agree a conversation occurred, and the content of that conversation is precisely what SAFE-1 sends to a person to read.

F4 is a post-trip written statement by the party with an interest in the outcome, and system-records priority cuts both ways: because no system record captures the spoken words, neither account wins automatically, which per SAFE-1 means no automated ruling and an escalation rather than a finding for the driver.

I do not contest that the route records are neutral (F1: 17.2 km vs 17.3 km optimal; F2: +2.3 min), and I claim no route or fare refund in this case; but a normal GPS track says nothing about what the driver said to the rider, and SAFE-1 is not limited to dangerous driving.

The driver's clean record (F6: 4.5 years, 4.86, 0 upheld disputes) is a mitigating factor for the reviewer to weigh, but it cannot substitute for the human assessment of the allegation itself, and no adverse account action is requested by me in this brief.

The rider's unblemished profile (F5: 3.8-year account, 4.8 rating, 0 disputes in 90 days) removes any suggestion of a bad-faith or serial complaint, so the sole-material point actually supports treating her contemporaneous safety report as credible enough for human review.

I agree with the disposition: escalate under SAFE-1 with a facts summary (F3, F4, F5, F6) — the summary must state that the rider alleged body comments and a request for her number, that she said she felt harassed and unsafe, and that the driver denies anything inappropriate, so the human reviewer sees both accounts.

Contested as to characterisation: F4 denies in substance that anything inappropriate happened — the driver says he made small talk only — so it is inaccurate to say he concedes the allegation; the words the rider attributes to him appear nowhere in any record, because F3 shows the chat record between the two contains no messages at all.

Conceded in outcome but not in framing: I likewise ask for escalate under SAFE-1, and I do not seek an automated finding either way; the difference between the parties is only that the rider treats the allegation as established while the file contains no record of the words said.

Accepted, and it cuts for the driver as much as the rider: F3 establishes the absence of any contemporaneous message containing body comments or a request for a number, so the only material before the reviewer is the unrecorded complaint set against the driver's denial in F4.

Agreed the objective records show no detour or overcharge (F1 shows 17.2 km against an optimal 17.3 km) and no evidence of dangerous driving on the timeline (F2 shows only a 2.3-minute overrun), so nothing in the trip data corroborates an unsafe ride.
Accepted: F5 shows a 3.8-year account, 4.8 rating and 0 disputes in 90 days, so there is no basis to attack the rider's good faith; that cuts both ways, and I make no such attack.

Agreed, and it should be given its full weight by the reviewer: F6 shows a 4.5-year account, 4.86 rating, 659 trips in 90 days and zero upheld disputes of any type, which is real evidence against a pattern of the conduct alleged and is a reason the reviewer should not default to an account action.
